gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly identifies the same false pointwise fractional Leibniz/product rule, gives a counterexample, and connects its failure to the unsupported nonlinear high-Sobolev estimate. Its proposed commutator-based replacement addresses the same failed operation.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose that the asserted pointwise fractional product decomposition is false and therefore cannot establish the uniform nonlinear energy estimate used for Galerkin analysis.

component_coverage.gold_component: The pointwise product/decomposition inequality is false, as shown by the explicit alpha=2 calculation, so the nonlinear high-Sobolev estimate and dependent arguments are unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states that the pointwise Leibniz inequality is false, demonstrates failure at alpha=2, identifies the resulting failure of the nonlinear energy estimate, and proposes a valid commutator/product-estimate replacement.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies that the local bound only holds to a lifespan depending on the current high Sobolev norm, and that restarting gives no uniform continuation time or global high-norm bound. This is the same failed iterative global-continuation argument as the gold issue.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the unsupported promotion of a norm-dependent local existence estimate into global strong well-posedness without a uniform all-time high-Sobolev bound or valid continuation criterion.

component_coverage.gold_component: The local lifespan depends on the high Sobolev norm, so restarting does not yield a uniform lower bound or an all-time H^{1+alpha} estimate; hence the global theorem is unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that bd3 is only local, that restarting may shrink the next lifespan, and that no global high-norm bound or continuation criterion is supplied; it therefore correctly limits the result to local existence unless a global bound is proved.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 recognizes an endpoint failure of W^{1,infinity} control in the nonlinear energy and uniqueness argument, but it does not diagnose the distinct spectral-error step involving the modified projection, its H^2-to-W^{1,infinity} estimate, and the resulting N-independent Gronwall coefficient. Mentioning the spectral proof as an affected consequence does not establish that specific missing estimate.

ISSUE-008 identifies that derivatives of the transformed vector field grow with N and that the proof lacks the derivative-count or commutator estimates needed for an N-uniform fifth-order remainder. Its repair directly requires uniform bounds for all derivatives entering that remainder.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the unsupported claim of an N-independent RK4 one-step O(Delta t^5) defect because the transformed vector-field derivatives and stage/remainder terms have not been uniformly bounded in N.

component_coverage.gold_component: The transformed-system/RK4 Taylor remainder contains high-order derivatives involving the order-(1+alpha) operator, and the proof does not establish bounds uniform in N; therefore the claimed uniform one-step defect is unsupported.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly notes N-growing frequencies in time derivatives, the absence of uniform derivative-count estimates, and the resulting failure of the N-independent local-error claim; it also proposes uniform bounds for the complete fifth-order remainder.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-009 identifies the missing nonlinear stability/Lipschitz estimate and uniform discrete error recursion needed to turn a local O(Delta t^5) defect into global O(Delta t^4) convergence. This is exactly the unsupported error-propagation step in the gold issue.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose that local consistency and a linearized stability result do not establish global nonlinear RK4 convergence; a uniform nonlinear flow-stability estimate and discrete Gronwall recursion are missing.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proof lacks comparison/stability of two nonlinear semidiscrete flows and therefore lacks an N-independent error-propagation recurrence; local defect plus linearized stability cannot prove the global fourth-order bound.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes local defect from global convergence, identifies the absence of nonlinear stability for the transformed quadratic system, and requires a uniform discrete Gronwall argument and timestep assumptions.
